A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GUI-agent distraction study, with matching scenarios, evaluation framework, and original results. All pages and displays are readable, including v2 Appendices A–C; v1 has no separate appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of ten agents on four simulated GUI scenarios, plus environment-injection experiments in Tables 3–8.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds DPO mitigation results in Table 9 and instruction-selection validation accuracy in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 adds a mitigation procedure absent from v1: mark the user's goal with special tokens, train instruction-channel preference using DPO, and apply the tags during inference. This introduces a training objective and inference intervention beyond the retained working patterns and button-rewriting attack.

E1.justification: v2 adds Alpaca-derived competing-instruction data for preference training and tagged-instruction validation. The original four GUI scenarios and their 1,198 samples remain unchanged; the mitigation experiment reuses the Pop-up box and Chat subsets.

E2.justification: The ten-agent comparisons in Tables 3–7 and GPT-4o/GLM-4v attack comparisons in Table 8 are unchanged. New Table 9 compares DPO-trained Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct against its original baseline and a preference-aware prompting variant.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a separate training-and-evaluation protocol: LoRA/DPO training on 3,200 examples for three epochs, followed by action-annotation evaluation on Pop-up box and Chat and an instruction-selection validation check. The original benchmark sizes, metrics, working patterns, and eight-goal attack evaluation remain unchanged. Newly disclosed decoding settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a specific error analysis of GPT-4o/GPT-4v CoT failures: agents skip dismissing pop-ups and select visible but unavailable background controls. The earlier SeeClick shortcut and scenario-comparison analyses are retained in Appendix A, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 adds accuracies and describes improvement as significant, but supplies no corresponding statistical uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 3–8 are numerically unchanged. New Table 9 reports baseline/prompt/DPO results: baseline-to-DPO Chat Accgold/Accdist changes from 31.8/61.8 to 40.9/53.6, while Pop-up box changes from 37.0/54.3 to 37.3/55.7. Appendix B.2 adds 96.5% tagged-instruction validation accuracy.

T1.justification: The substantive state/action definitions, matching rules, accuracy measures, and working-pattern equations remain equivalent. Removing the EPISODE notation and expressing the existing attack procedure through Equation 11 do not introduce new mathematical reasoning. Neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about environmental distraction, insufficient protection from stronger perception, and exploitable unfaithfulness are retained. v2 broadens the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to include an input-preference approach for improving faithfulness, extending v1's diagnostic and attack-focused contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: Appendix A.2 develops the blocked-control and cross-modal reasoning explanation; Section 5.2 interprets DPO's differing behavior across subsets; and the Limitations section and Appendix C discuss incomplete scenario coverage, unmeasured consequence severity, and constraints on self-correction.

D1.justification: Where v1 deferred prompts and detailed implementation to a future release, v2 Appendix B supplies working-pattern prompts, a distraction-generation prompt, decoding and image-handling settings, and DPO data construction and hyperparameters. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although v1's Lucene indexing and category-restricted retrieval details are omitted. The stated code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the generic MLLM background subsection and associated citations while adding literature on instruction prioritization, preference training, visual reasoning, and agent safety. Appendix C.2 substantively positions the study against newer environmental attacks, including Liao et al. and Zhang et al., distinguishing their threat assumptions from the benign distraction setting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and methodology undergo extensive rewriting. v1 Section 5's diagnostic analyses move to Appendix A, the attack study becomes Section 5.1, and v2 adds a mitigation section, explicit Limitations, and implementation/discussion appendices. The title and affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes displays: the example screenshots and scenario-feature figure move into the appendix and exchange figure numbers; the attack-algorithm box becomes Equation 11; and a simulation algorithm, Table 9, and six framed prompt/data examples are added. The original four figures and Tables 1–8 retain their substantive contents.

improvement.justification: The newly supplied prompts/settings, targeted error analysis, and explicit limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. The added mitigation experiment provides useful but mixed evidence: Chat improves, whereas Pop-up Accdist rises from 54.3 to 55.7 despite prose describing modest improvement. The original benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the new experiment lacks uncertainty reporting, limiting the overall quality gain.
